text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed the autoscaler is spinning up N4x-large nodes in us-west-2 even when there are spare small-gpu pools available. Cost spike this morning. anyone seen this pattern?
josh: I saw that too. Pods with nodeAffinity for "gpu-type: any" are getting scheduled onto the big pool. Suspect expander choice + binpacking mismatch. :thinking:
ankur: Do we still have --expander=least-waste set? I thought we moved to binpack for throughput clusters.
kevin: It's set to least-waste on the clusters handling trainer+inference mixed workloads. Reason was to avoid lots of tiny nodes during training bursts.
maria: The problem is heterogenous pools: small-gpu (cheap preemptible), large-gpu (on-demand). Least-waste is preferring large to fit multi-gpu pods, but many inference pods could fit on small-gpu if we respected pod resourceRequests better.
sre-oncall: Deploy bot shows these events:
```
deploy-bot: autoscaler: scaleUp: triggered by pending pods (inference-svc x6)
autoscaler: created node group pool-large-gpu count +3 (provisioning)
```
kevin: Also saw scale-down failing because of system pods with hostPath mounts. We have --skip-nodes-with-local-storage true, so those nodes get sticky and autoscaler won't touch them until kubelet evicts.
ankur: Can we tune --scale-down-unneeded-time and --scale-down-utilization-threshold? Right now util threshold is 0.5 and unneeded-time 10m. Lower threshold might allow more aggressive consolidation.
josh: Danger: aggressive scale-down bumps latency for warm caches. For inference we rely on prefix KV cache. If we destroy nodes too quickly, we pay cold-start costs. Maybe different policies per node pool?
maria: Agreed. Proposal: 1) set --expander=price-aware (prototype) or swap to binpack for inference-only clusters, 2) add nodeSelector/taints to steer inference pods to small-gpu pool (taint: inference=true:NoSchedule), 3) reduce --max-node-provision-time to 5m to avoid long provisioning on large instances, 4) lower --scale-down-unneeded-time to 5m for bursty training pools.
kevin: For (1) we don't have price-aware out of the box. Could add a webhook that annotates nodes with "cost/score" and use a custom expander. Or use CA's node group weights via metadata to bias binpack selection.
ankur: Another quick win: set --balance-similar-node-groups and adjust nodeGroup auto-scaling priorities so CA prefers consolidating within the same family before creating big nodes.
sre-oncall: Also saw cross-zone scheduling constraints — some pods have anti-affinity which prevents spreading onto small-gpu nodes in the same AZ. Check pod topologySpreadConstraints.
josh: Good call. I found several helm charts defaulting to spread across zones. That pushes CA to create new capacity in another zone (expensive). We should change charts to zone-aware affinity for inference.
maria: Action items:
- kevin: prototype a small admission webhook that tags pending pods with preferred-pool based on labels (due EOD).
- ankur: test lowering --scale-down-unneeded-time to 5m in staging and capture latency/regression (due tomorrow).
- josh: audit charts for topologySpread/default anti-affinity and submit PRs to tighten spreads for inference (due today).
- sre-oncall: watch for scale events and post anomalies to #incidents if cost > $X/hr.
kevin: I'll also add a CloudWatch/GCP metric for node provisioning time so we can tune --max-node-provision-time empirically.
ankur: If we need more complex logic, we could run a small controller that computes a weighted score: (fit_score - cost_score) and set nodeGroup priorities. That keeps CA simple and lets us iterate.
maria: Sounds good. One more: add a short-runbook on when to create dedicated inference pools vs mixing. Right now it's fuzzy.
sre-oncall: Noted. will create a runbook draft. :memo:
josh: Thanks all. I'll monitor cost dashboard and post an update tomorrow morning. :rocket:
